messages:
jun (eng-runtime): Heads up - CI perf alert just came in for the nightly quantization job. throughput down ~28% on int4 workload after merge of PR #4292 :alarm_clock:

samir: saw that. reproducing locally on a small cluster now — looks like a routing fallback is triggering a slow path repeatedly.

elaine: any obvious suspects? kernel selection change or batching heuristic?

samir: 90% confidence it's the batching scheduler change in #4292 + the new routing predicate from #4307. behavior: when small prompt lengths interleave with long ones, requests keep being routed to the "fallback" pipeline that uses dequant->fp path.

kyle: repro script? can we get a flamegraph?

samir: paste logs from local run: ```
[2026-03-18T09:12:23Z] req=0x7f8fa kvcache: hit
[2026-03-18T09:12:23Z] req=0x7f8fa kernel_select: chose=q4r_fast
[2026-03-18T09:12:23Z] req=0x7f8fa route: fallback=True -> dequant_path
[2026-03-18T09:12:23Z] latency_ms=32 dequant_ms=21
[2026-03-18T09:12:23Z] req=0x7f8fb kernel_select: chose=q4r_fast
[2026-03-18T09:12:23Z] req=0x7f8fb route: fallback=True -> dequant_path
[2026-03-18T09:12:23Z] latency_ms=30 dequant_ms=19
```
Summary: kernel selected low-precision path but routing logic bails to dequant fallback every other request, so KV cache locality is destroyed and dequant overhead dominates.

elaine: interesting - so kernel selection isn't the issue per se; it's routing+batcher ordering that causes thrash. could explain the 28% throughput loss.

jun (eng-runtime): Which commits to bisect? Is #4292 the merge we suspect?

samir: suspect range: from merge 2026-03-10 -> 2026-03-16. includes #4258 (kv prefetch tweak), #4292 (batch scheduler rewrite), #4307 (route predicate refactor). I'd start with #4292.

kyle: +1. I'll run a bisect across those three on canary infra (small fleet) and post perf numbers.

deploy-bot: nightly-quant-ci failed: job=quant-int4-throughput, delta=-28.4%, artifact=https://ci.internal/runs/2891/artifact/profile.pb

samir: quick mitigation: we could add a conservative guard in routing to prefer current instance's cache affinity and avoid fallback for sub-ms delta. patch is tiny. want to ship a canary revert or a guard?

elaine: prefer guard — less risky than revert. also add telemetry: route_reason + kvcache_age to trace these flips.

jun (eng-runtime): agree on guard + telemetry. PR draft?

samir: PR: draft at https://git.redwood/eng/runtime/pulls/4312 - adds `route.prefers_affinity` and toggles fallback threshold to 2.5ms. includes test sim for mixed prompt-lengths.

kyle: running canary with that patch now. will report TTFB and tokens/s after 30m.

jun (eng-runtime): if canary shows <5% regression lock, we can queue the guard for staged rollout. if not, revert #4292.

samir: also queued a bisect run isolating #4292 -> #4292^ (pre-merge). starting now.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy queued: service=runtime-canary, change=eng/runtime@4312, cohort=5nodes

kyle: first 10m numbers: tokens/s up 12% vs failing run (so guard helps), p50 latency down ~8% for mixed workloads. kvcache hit-rate recovered from 62% -> 89%.

elaine: great. add a follow-up to revert the scheduling rewrite in #4292 if we can't find a clean fix; but for now ship the guard + telemetry.

jun (eng-runtime): filing the rollout ticket and an eval to check quality delta for q4r profile (we must ensure guard doesn't change quant selection outcomes).

samir: note for postmortem: quantify dequant cost per token when fallback flips, and add unit tests for batcher ordering with kvcache affinity.

kyle: logging artifact from canary: https://storage.internal/canary/4312/trace.log (contains route_reason histograms).

jun (eng-runtime): thanks everyone — moving to staged rollout with monitoring. will update #eng-runtime in 1h with final numbers. :thumbsup:
